name: neurological localization overview
title: Approach to a neurological problem: describe it (onset, course, deficits), localize the lesion (cortex, subcortex or brainstem from the brain pearls; the list of places that weaken both legs; dysarthria and the cerebellar system for slurred speech), then let the tempo predict the type of lesion for the differential

root.title: 1 · DESCRIBE → 2 · LOCALIZE → 3 · DIFFERENTIAL
lines: describe: onset (acute, subacute, chronic) · progressive, intermittent or stable · deficits (cognitive, motor, sensory, coordination)
the TEMPO predicts the lesion: hyperacute → ischemic stroke, hemorrhage · acute → trauma · subacute → inflammation, infection, tumour · chronic → tumour
localizing helps plan the right investigations · upper or lower motor neuron (UMN, LMN) weakness: see the WEAKNESS chart

groups.title: BRAIN SIGNS: which part of the brain?

head: h
Cortex
cortical signs
where: Middle cerebral artery (MCA): face + arm >> leg
• no speech, follows commands, right face + arm weak → LEFT frontal lobe

head: h
Brainstem
intrinsic brainstem lesion
where: hemiparesis + cranial nerve or cerebellar findings: see the WEAKNESS chart

head: h
Bilateral leg weakness
where: • examine for a SENSORY LEVEL to aim the imaging

head: h
Dysarthria
slurred speech
where: • CNS: cortex (mouth area), subcortex, thalamus, brainstem, cerebellum
• PNS: nerve (recurrent laryngeal), neuromuscular junction (myasthenia), muscle
• the company decides: cranial nerves, UMN or LMN, weakness, ataxia, sensory

head: h
Cerebellar system
coordinates all movement
where: → right cerebellum, or its pathway (internal capsule, thalamus, pons)
